_meta.indication: EMRELIS is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic, non-squamous NSCLC with high c-Met protein overexpression (≥ 50% of tumor cells with strong (3+) staining), as determined by an FDA-approved test, who have received a prior systemic therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, single-arm, non-randomized, multi-cohort trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with previously treated, locally advanced or metastatic, EGFR wild-type non-squamous NSCLC with high c-Met protein overexpression (≥ 50% of tumor cells with strong (3+) staining)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 by blinded independent central review; additional endpoint duration of response (DOR)
pivotal_trials.n: Primary efficacy population N=84 (EGFR WT high c-Met overexpression)
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed ORR 35% (95% CI 24, 46); all partial responses (CR 0%); median DOR 7.2 months (95% CI 4.2, 12) among 29 responders; DOR ≥ 6 months 59%, DOR ≥ 12 months 21%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%): peripheral neuropathy (51%; Grade 3-4 11%), fatigue (29%), decreased appetite (22%), peripheral edema (22%). Serious adverse reactions in 35% of patients; fatal adverse reactions in 5%, including ILD/pneumonitis (1.8%).
target_moa: c-Met-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC): humanized IgG1κ anti-c-Met antibody conjugated via a protease-cleavable linker to MMAE, a microtubule-disrupting agent; after binding c-Met-expressing cells it is internalized and releases MMAE, causing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.

rems.type: No REMS required; safety concerns were determined to be adequately addressed through labeling.

companion_dx_detail: VENTANA MET (SP44) RxDx Assay, a qualitative IHC assay approved as a companion diagnostic to identify non-squamous NSCLC patients with high c-Met protein overexpression (≥ 50% of tumor cells with strong (3+) staining) eligible for treatment.

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee, as no significant efficacy or safety issues requiring external input were identified.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR); ORR is an intermediate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit in NSCLC.

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) [see *Clinical Studies* (14)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).

ORR is a direct measure of the intervention, as in the absence of therapy, NSCLC tumors do not typically regress; for NSCLC, ORR is considered an intermediate endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

requirement.text: 4844-2 Complete clinical trial, Study M25-274, "A Phase 2, Open-Label, Randomized, Global Study of Three Telisotuzumab Vedotin Regimens in Subjects with Previously Treated c-Met Overexpressing, EGFR Wildtype, Locally Advanced/Metastatic Non-Squamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer" to further assess known serious risks with telisotuzumab vedotin including interstitial lung disease, ocular disorders, and other severe adverse reactions, evaluating alternative dosages (flat dosage 1.9 mg/kg Q2W vs flat dosage 1.6 mg/kg Q2W vs. 1.6 mg/kg → 1.9 mg/kg Q2W dose up-titration).
